note: GLOBALCIT's Citizenship Law Dataset v3.0 (EUI, 2025), coding the law in force on 1 January 2024 (A06a NET 8(1); A06b NET 8(1); L05 NET 15(1)(a), 16(1)(e)): ordinary naturalisation after 5 years' residence; the applicant must give up other citizenships (with major exceptions); a citizen loses the citizenship on voluntarily taking another (with exceptions). Reforms after that date are checked in the file's later sources, where a later source is given. The Kingdom Act as consolidated today still asks five years' admission and principal residence immediately before the request (art. 8(1)(c)).

sources.title: GLOBALCIT Citizenship Law Dataset v3.0 (Vink, van der Baaren, Bauböck, Dzankic, Honohan, Manby; EUI Research Data, 2025), country-year-mode files, Netherlands, 2024
sources.said: Person has been resident in the Netherlands for 5 years immediately before the application and there are no objections against indefinite residence in the country. ... Renunciation or automatic loss of citizenship of another country (with exceptions). ... Person voluntarily acquires citizenship of another country. Provision does not apply if person is born and resides in another country, or resided in another country for 5 years before majority, or is married to a citizen of another country (adults), or his/her parent is citizen of the Netherlands (minors), or acquired citizenship by birth in the Netherlands. No exception to main rule if Article 1 of 1963 Strasbourg Convention applies.
